concerns.text: T051 mandates bootstrap resampling to flag 'Unstable' correlations, but Spec SC-004 explicitly defines robustness as a 'threshold sweep' (p < 0.01, 0.05, 0.10) with rank stability. T051 replaces the mandated verification method with an unauthorized statistical technique, violating the success criterion defined in the spec.

T051 duplicates the artifact generation of T031 (sensitivity_report.csv) but attempts to inject a different 'Unstable' flag logic. This creates a conflict where the same output file is defined by two mutually exclusive verification methods (sweep vs. bootstrap), violating the single-source-of-truth for verification logic.

T014 verifies recovery of a fixed ground truth (r=0.6) but fails to implement the FR-007 requirement to 'report the minimum detectable effect size' for the specific N=50 sample. The task focuses on validating a known value rather than quantifying the study's power for other potential effect sizes, weakening the FR-007 deliverable.

T016b (Synthetic Graph Builder) does not explicitly mandate verification that the generated synthetic data respects the Voronoi edge definition (Constitution Principle VII) before graph construction. The task relies on 'pymatgen/ase neighbors' which may default to distance cutoffs if not explicitly forced to Voronoi, risking a silent violation of the graph-theoretic fidelity constraint.

T049 requires a strict checksum validation against a 'pre-calculated' hash X for synthetic data. This violates Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) which states 'No data may be modified in place' and requires checksums to reflect content derivation. Hard-coding a static hash for a generative algorithm creates a fragility point where any algorithmic change (even a bug fix) breaks the checksum, violating the spirit of data hygiene.
